t:
None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2013 for research, development, test, and evaluation for the Next Generation Foundry for the Defense Microelectronics Activity (PE #603720S) may be obligated or expended for that purpose until a period of 60 days has elapsed following the date on which the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering—
    (1) develops a microelectronics strategy as described in the Senate report to accompany S. 1253 of the 112th Congress (S. Rept. 112–26) and an estimate of the full life-cycle costs for the upgrade of the Next Generation Foundry; 
    (2) develops an assessment regarding the manufacturing capability of the United States to produce three-dimensional integrated circuits to serve national defense interests; and 
    (3) submits to the congressional defense committees the strategy and cost estimate required by paragraph (1) and the assessment required by paragraph (2).

fable.w: The section conditions funding on a federal official developing a strategy and assessment and submitting them to congressional defense committees. The tempting reading is that the submission and waiting period amount to a consultative process, but Congress is inside the federal government, so this is purely intra-governmental reporting. No state, public, expert, or industry party is consulted or given a role in any federal decision.
fable.s: submits to the congressional defense committees the strategy and cost estimate required by paragraph (1) and the assessment required by paragraph (2).

opus.w: The only process in this section is a report from a Defense Department official to the congressional defense committees, followed by a 60-day waiting period before funds can be spent. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is not participation. No states, experts, the public or other outside parties are consulted. The section looks procedural, but every actor in it is federal.
opus.s: submits to the congressional defense committees the strategy and cost estimate required by paragraph (1) and the assessment required by paragraph (2)
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes": the section sets up a formal step (a strategy, a cost estimate and an assessment, plus a 60-day wait) before funds can be spent. That reading fails because the only interaction is the Assistant Secretary submitting documents to the congressional defense committees. Congress is inside the federal government, and no outside party is consulted.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Assistant Secretary of Defense to develop a strategy and assessment and submit them to congressional defense committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is internal coordination, not participation with outside parties. The text does not mandate consultation with states, tribes, the public, or private entities before making the decision to obligate funds.
qwen_chat.s: submits to the congressional defense committees the strategy and cost estimate required by paragraph (1) and the assessment required by paragraph (2)
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the strategy and assessment involve "national defense interests" and "manufacturing capability," they implicitly require input from outside experts or industry. However, the text itself only mandates that the Assistant Secretary *develops* these documents and *submits* them to Congress. It does not explicitly require consultation with non-federal entities. Furthermore, the submission is to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government.
